atom:feed.atom:subtitle: Preview, pending Avi’s review

atom:entry.atom:title: NZ moves on commercial cards
atom:entry.atom:summary: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower regulated commercial-card interchange is coming; confirm what your acquirer passes through. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The 22 October decision introduces commercial credit-card interchange limits on Mastercard and Visa. Who: New Zealand merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2027-04-22. Official source: https://www.comcom.govt.nz/regulated-industries/projects/interchange-fee-regulation/

atom:entry.atom:title: Scheme fees come into view
atom:entry.atom:summary: [deadline] So what for merchants: Use the new scheme-fee disclosures to challenge unexplained line items. Preview, pending Avi’s review. First quarterly aggregate fee publications by designated card networks were due for the July–September period. Who: Card networks; acquiring teams. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Acquirer fee disclosures begin
atom:entry.atom:summary: [deadline] So what for merchants: Compare published acquirer fees with your own card mix and contract. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Qualifying large acquirers must publish merchant service fee data by merchant size and card type. Who: Large acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2026-10-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Australia: card surcharge reset
atom:entry.atom:summary: [neutral] So what for merchants: Recheck checkout pricing: designated card-network surcharge rules changed. Preview, pending Avi’s review. eftpos, Mastercard and Visa no-surcharge rules apply from 1 October after the RBA removed its prohibition on those rules. Who: Australian merchants and acquirers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/faqs/index.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Domestic interchange: lower caps
atom:entry.atom:summary: [cost down] So what for merchants: Lower domestic interchange caps make pass-through worth checking; net merchant savings depend on your terms. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Revised interchange regulation applies to domestic-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Australian acquirers and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Issuer compensation rules change
atom:entry.atom:summary: [neutral] So what for merchants: Check issuer incentives against the amended compensation rules. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The amended net-compensation regime starts, with transitional arrangements for 2026/27. Who: Card networks and issuers. Effective: 2026-10-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Next: prove interchange pass-through
atom:entry.atom:summary: [deadline] So what for merchants: Ask your acquirer how the interchange reduction reached your statement. Preview, pending Avi’s review. First publication of large acquirers’ interchange pass-through measures covers October–December 2026. Who: Large acquirers and merchant finance teams. Effective: 2027-01-30. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Foreign-issued cards get a cap
atom:entry.atom:summary: [deadline] So what for merchants: Review foreign-card pricing before the new caps apply. Preview, pending Avi’s review. Interchange caps extend to foreign-issued card transactions acquired in Australia. Who: Cross-border acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Merchant statements get sharper
atom:entry.atom:summary: [deadline] So what for merchants: Make sure the new statement detail reaches your reconciliation process. Preview, pending Avi’s review. More statement detail is required from the first full statement period starting on or after 1 April. Who: Australian acquirers and merchants. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html

atom:entry.atom:title: Scheme-fee roadmap expected
atom:entry.atom:summary: [neutral] So what for merchants: Watch for the fee roadmap; it is not itself a price cap. Preview, pending Avi’s review. The RBA expects a scheme-fee roadmap by 1 April; this is an expectation, not a new fee cap. Who: Card networks and acquiring teams. Effective: 2027-04-01. Official source: https://www.rba.gov.au/payments-and-infrastructure/review-of-retail-payments-regulation/2026-03/conclusions-paper/impact-and-implementation.html
